note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors. Nominations were received by Mr. James M'Cammon, deputy returning officer, on Tuesday 5 May 1936: 'There are sixteen electoral divisions which return members, and in respect of thirteen of these nominations were handed in'; there were no contests. No nomination was received for Beaghmore, Pomeroy or Slatequarry, whose retiring members were deemed re-elected (Mid-Ulster Mail, 9 May 1936, p. 9). Polling in County Tyrone was fixed for Wednesday 3 June 1936 (Strabane Chronicle, 21 March 1936, p. 4; Belfast News-Letter, 17 March 1936, p. 12); no poll was needed. Filed on 1936-06-03, the Tyrone polling day (previously filed under 1936-05-28, 6 Nov 2026). No nomination; the retiring member, named in the election's report, was deemed re-elected. Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
